text:
mike.s: Heads up — found 4 uploads to redwood-backups with no SSE metadata. Looks like cleartext at rest. Example: s3://redwood-backups/db/tenant123/2026-03-20.dump — head-object shows no x-amz-server-side-encryption header.
sara_r: Wat. are these from the uploader service or the old backup agent?
mike.s: head-object shows owner=iam-uploader-prod. Running CloudTrail lookup now. Also noticed CMK id in bucket policy != expected key id.
henry_g: We rolled a small RBAC change to the uploader role last night (terraform). @katie_prodsec added s3:PutObject to the role — could be related.
katie_prodsec: I added s3:PutObject but missed kms:Encrypt and didn't add PutObjectAcl permissions. The uploader is supposed to set SSE headers client-side; I forgot to grant it the KMS grant. Sorry. :sweat_smile:
mike.s: That explains it — uploads succeed but without SSE-CMK, so objects landed unencrypted. Need immediate containment + triage.
henry_g: oncall — can you revoke PutObject for iam-uploader-prod while we triage? encops-bot: please open an incident if we revoke.
encops-bot: Incident created: RBAC-2026-03-20-S3-UnencryptedUploads — routed to encops-oncall.
oncall: Revoked PutObject for iam-uploader-prod. Kicked off inventory scan across redwood-backups to find affected keys. ETA ~12m.
sara_r: CloudTrail shows PutObject events for the same timeframe where requestParameters.serverSideEncryption is null. Quick query: eventName=PutObject AND requestParameters.serverSideEncryption=null
mike.s: Scan found 54 objects across multiple tenant prefixes. Proposal: re-encrypt by copying objects with --sse aws:kms and the correct key id to a new prefix, update inventory, then delete originals. Example copy cmd: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/db/tenant123/2026-03-20.dump s3://redwood-backups-encrypted/db/tenant123/2026-03-20.dump --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```
Any object ownership issues we should consider before copying?
katie_prodsec: Agree on re-encrypt. I'll open a terraform PR to add kms:Encrypt to the uploader role and add a bucket policy that denies PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is missing. Also will add a pre-check in CI.
henry_g: We'll patch the uploader agent to fail uploads when SSE header is absent and emit metric uploader.upload_missing_sse. Rolling a canary today.
mike.s: Risk assessment — bucket is private (not public), so exposure is internal. Still high-risk: internal staff or compromised service accounts with GetObject could have read backups. Suggest rotating credentials/secrets for affected tenants and inform Legal/Privacy.
katie_prodsec: I'll draft customer notice and loop in legal. Also adding a bucket policy condition to enforce server-side encryption at put-time.
oncall: Scan finished; 54 objects identified. Starting re-encrypt job now using the copy workflow to encrypted prefix.
mike.s: Action items: katie — open infra PR (add kms grant + bucket deny policy), henry — uploader agent patch and metric, oncall — complete re-encrypt and produce CSV of affected object keys, sara — run final audit query and verify no new unencrypted puts. Tagging #inc-1234.
katie_prodsec: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8123 — adds kms:Encrypt to uploader role, bucket deny policy, and a pre-deploy check.
henry_g: Agent patch pushed to canary; metric added. If canary looks good will roll to prod in 30m.
mike.s: Once re-encrypts complete we'll restore PutObject for uploader and monitor. Keep incident open until PR merged and customer comms done. :thumbsup:
